title: Vasco and Cruzeiro: decisive clash for the Brasileirão
seoTitle: Vasco vs Cruzeiro: decisive Brazilian Serie A clash
subtitle: Teams with different objectives face off at São Januário, with nationwide broadcast.
excerpt: On Saturday (29), Vasco and Cruzeiro clash in the 25th round of the Brazilian Championship, with the Cruzmaltino battling relegation and the Cabuloso aiming for.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Vasco and Cruzeiro meet this Saturday (29) in a match that shakes up the Brasileirão and pits teams with opposite goals against each other. The 25th‑round showdown comes at a crucial moment for both clubs, generating great interest among fans.

Where to watch the decisive clash

The encounter between Vasco and Cruzeiro will be broadcast nationwide by RECORD, starting at 8:55 p.m. For the East and Northeast of Minas Gerais, the exclusive free‑to‑air transmission will be on TV Leste RECORD. On digital platforms, fans can follow the game on R7.com and RecordPlus. Commentary will be provided by Cleber Machado, with analysis from Maurício Noriega, Dodô and Sálvio Spinola. Presentation will be handled by Paloma Tocci and Bruno Laurence, while Gabriela Marino and Bruno Piccinato will bring live reports from Estádio São Januário in Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

Vasco's fight against relegation

Vasco takes the field in a delicate situation in the Brasileirão, sitting in 19th place with 23 points, inside the relegation zone. The club needs a win over the Minas Gerais rival to try to climb out of the bottom four. Led by Portuguese coach Pedro Emanuel, the team is enduring an eight‑match winless streak in the league, with two draws and six defeats. In the most recent games, the Cruzmaltino was outplayed by Santos and Palmeiras, both by three‑goal margins. Vasco's last league victory came in the 15th round, still under the command of Renato Gaúcho.

Cruzeiro eyes a Libertadores spot

On the other side, Cruzeiro is experiencing a different moment in the competition. The Minas Gerais side sits near the top of the table, in fifth place with 39 points, opening a qualification spot for the next edition of the CONMEBOL Libertadores. The Cabuloso is two points behind fourth‑placed Fluminense and two points ahead of Bahia, which occupies sixth. Under Portuguese manager Artur Jorge, the team arrives on a wave of four consecutive league wins, achieved against Coritiba (1‑0), Mirassol (3‑1), Corinthians (2‑1) and Flamengo (2‑1). Since the competition resumed after the World Cup, Cruzeiro has suffered only one defeat, a 1‑0 loss to Botafogo.

Probable line‑ups and absences

Coach Pedro Emanuel is expected to make changes to the Vasco side that beat Vitória 1‑0 in the first leg of the Copa do Brasil quarter‑finals. Players such as Paulo Henrique, Cuiabano and Sosa should return to the starting eleven. Robert Renan is a doubt for the match. The main uncertainties lie in midfield and attack, with Ramon Rique competing with Tchê Tchê, and Adson, Spinelli and David fighting for the final attacking spot, with Adson favored. The likely Vasco line‑up includes Léo Jardim; Paulo Henrique, Cuesta, Lucas Freitas and Cuiabano; Sosa, Tchê Tchê (Ramon Rique) and Thiago Mendes; Andrés Gómez, Colidio and Adson (Spinelli).

Clash of Brazilian quadruple champions

The São Januário showdown also features two clubs with a victorious history in the Brasileirão. Both Vasco and Cruzeiro are four‑time national champions. The Cruzmaltino lifted the trophy in 1974, 1989, 1997 and 2000. The Raposa won it in 1966, 2003, 2013 and 2014. Moreover, both clubs are led by Portuguese coaches—Pedro Emanuel at Vasco and Artur Jorge at Cruzeiro—adding an extra spice to the encounter.

Information from GE, R7.
